assessment.nobel_worthiness: Flat bands at the magic angle and the resulting correlated insulators and superconductivity opened an entirely new, tunable platform for strongly correlated electrons. The prediction was quantitative and the experiments were decisive and clean; the originality and breadth of follow-on work are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model predicted the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the 2018 experimental discovery of correlated states and superconductivity. Theory plus experiment supports a clean three-person split, though the credit of the experimental team (including Cao) and Kim and Dean groups' parallel work is not fully captured.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups reproduced the phases within a few years, but the origin of the superconductivity and the nature of the correlated states remain debated; recognition is timely if the committee accepts that mechanism need not be settled for the discovery itself.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism and the ground states are not settled.
Credit for the experimental discovery involves junior co-authors outside the supplied names.
I cannot independently verify reproducibility details beyond my recollection.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance and the later giant MgO-based TMR made spin-dependent tunnelling a practical effect, underpinning hard-disk read heads and magnetic random-access memory. Close to my own field of magnetism and spin transport, the discovery is clear and has had very large technological impact.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera independently reported room-temperature TMR in 1995; Parkin's group, and the Yuasa/Djayaprawira work on coherent MgO tunnelling, drove the giant values. The three named people are plausible, but the MgO coherent-tunnelling contribution may deserve separate credit and the 2007 GMR prize overlaps in spirit.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed and in mass-market devices for roughly two decades, so recognition is overdue rather than premature. The Nobel Committee previously honoured GMR, which raises a question of novelty relative to the earlier prize.
uncertainties: Whether the MgO coherent-tunnelling work by others outweighs the 1995 discovery in the credit split.
Overlap with the GMR prize may be judged as incremental.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Correcting spherical aberration in electron lenses overcame a limit recognised since Scherzer and delivered sub-angstrom imaging of atoms, which is now central to materials physics, including the study of magnetic and two-dimensional systems. This is an invention of clear and lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Rose supplied the theory of the multipole corrector, Haider and Urban built and demonstrated the working corrector in the TEM, and Urban led the application to materials. The configuration is natural; contributions by Krivanek on STEM correction are outside the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Commercially routine and widely confirmed for around two decades; the recognition is mature and, if anything, late.
uncertainties: Parallel STEM-corrector work by others is not credited in the supplied names.
Some may view this as instrumentation rather than a physics discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Z2 classification of the quantum spin Hall insulator and its experimental realisation in HgTe wells created the field of topological band insulators and altered how we think about electronic structure. The originality is high, and it ties band theory to topology, which as a first-principles theorist I find compelling.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the decisive theory; Molenkamp's group with the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal measured the effect. The supplied credit omits Zhang and Bernevig, and the 3D materials from Hasan and others add further claimants, so the allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in multiple materials and by independent groups for well over a decade. The 2016 prize honoured topological phases, so another award in this area needs a clear separation.
uncertainties: Allocation among Kane-Mele, BHZ, Molenkamp, 3D topological insulators and Hasan's group is unresolved.
Overlap with the 2016 topological phase prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock with magic-wavelength trapping reached fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and opens tests of fundamental constants and relativistic geodesy. It is a clean and important instrumentation advance.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and Ye drove the best performance and its many-body developments. The two-person allocation looks fair, though ion-clock groups and Hall/Hansch comb prize precedent affect framing.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs confirm performance and a redefinition of the second is under discussion, so timing is favourable.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with earlier recognition of frequency combs and ion clocks.
Redefinition of the SI second has not yet occurred.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory gave the first controlled non-perturbative framework for the Mott transition and, combined with density functional theory, a route to realistic correlated materials. Having used these methods myself, I regard it as foundational for modern correlated-electron theory.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt's infinite-dimension limit and Georges and Kotliar's mapping onto an impurity problem were both decisive; the supplied names omit Metzner and Müller-Hartmann, so the credit is partly incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted for three decades, though the accuracy in low dimensions and for realistic materials is still a limited-trust approximation. The idea is mature.
uncertainties: Omitted early contributors, notably Metzner, complicate a fair three-person prize.
Theoretical rather than a discrete experimental discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2008 discovery of superconductivity in LaFeAsO(1-x)Fx led to a second family of high-temperature superconductors beyond the cuprates, which sparked an enormous theoretical and experimental effort in correlated-electron physics.
assessment.attribution: The discovery paper is attributable to Hosono's group, so a single laureate is defensible. Subsequent critical-temperature increases by Chinese groups and early work on the material class are outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced rapidly and extensively; the pairing mechanism is still contested and no application has matured, which tempers the case.
uncertainties: Credit for the rapid follow-on Tc raise by other groups is not in the supplied name.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultrasoft pseudopotentials and the projector augmented-wave method made plane-wave density-functional calculations accurate and efficient across the periodic table, and they underlie a large share of present materials computation, including magnetic and correlated systems. The impact is vast though it is methods rather than a physical discovery.
assessment.attribution: Vanderbilt introduced ultrasoft pseudopotentials, Blöchl the PAW formalism, and Kresse and Joubert the practical implementation in VASP; the three names capture the central line but not Joubert or the all-electron method developers whose work overlaps.
assessment.maturity: Decades of use confirm robustness, but the 1998 chemistry prize for density functional theory and the usual preference for discoveries over computational tools suggest a Physics prize here is uncertain.
uncertainties: As a computational methodology it may fall outside the Physics prize's preference for discovery or invention.
Credit allocation relative to Joubert and all-electron developers is unresolved.
I have a field-based familiarity with these methods that may bias my view.
